title: Definition of Done
sub: When is a story truly complete
lifecycle: Living — reviewed every 3 sprints or at retrospectives
doel: Create shared understanding of "done" so stories are consistently and completely delivered.
template:
# Definition of Done

Version: [date] | From sprint: [N]

## Code
- [ ] Code reviewed by ≥1 peer
- [ ] No new linting errors
- [ ] Unit tests written and passing
- [ ] No TODO/FIXME in code

## Functionality
- [ ] All ACs verified by tester
- [ ] Happy path and edge cases tested
- [ ] Tested in staging

## Non-Functional
- [ ] Response time within NFR targets
- [ ] No new security vulnerabilities
- [ ] Logging added for key operations

## Documentation
- [ ] API contract updated if changed
- [ ] ADR written if architectural decision made
- [ ] Release notes entry added

## Task Quality
- [ ] No single implementation task exceeded 8h
- [ ] All tasks have a clear done-when criterion

## Process
- [ ] PO has accepted the story
- [ ] Story moved to Done in backlog tool

## Feature Handoff Ceremony (end of feature, not per story)
- [ ] Spec walkthrough done with dev team
- [ ] Task sequence agreed and parallel tasks identified
- [ ] All open questions in Clarification Log resolved
- [ ] Test environment ready
- [ ] Stakeholder sign-off received
- [ ] Consistency Analysis gate: PASS

aiTasks.name: DoD Reviewer
aiTasks.objective: Review DoD against industry standards and flag vague or unverifiable items.
aiTasks.prompt: You are an Agile Coach. Review this DoD: (1) Are items objectively binary (pass/fail)? (2) Are categories missing (security, observability, documentation)? (3) Are items too broad? Suggest a revised DoD with specific, verifiable criteria.

aiTasks.name: Risk Flagger
aiTasks.objective: Identify stories with unresolved dependencies or vague ACs that risk non-completion.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Scrum Master. For each committed story, flag: (1) ACs not approved, (2) unresolved tech dependencies, (3) stakeholder unavailability, (4) underestimated complexity. Output: Story | Risk | Action.

aiTasks.name: Stakeholder Summary Writer
aiTasks.objective: Rewrite technical release notes in plain language for non-technical stakeholders.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a BA skilled in stakeholder communication. Rewrite these release notes in plain, non-technical language. Focus on: what the user can do now, how it improves their experience, known limitations. Max 3 sentences per feature. No jargon.

title: Test Plan
sub: Test scope, approach, and test cases
lifecycle: Per feature or release — created before development starts on a feature
trigger: Feature approved and before sprint development begins
doel: Define what will be tested, how, and by whom — before development starts — so quality is built in, not checked at the end.
note: A test plan written before development guides implementation. Writing it after development is a test report, not a test plan.
template:

aiTasks.name: Test Case Generator
aiTasks.objective: Generate comprehensive test cases from the ACs and feature description.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a QA Engineer. Based on the ACs and feature description, generate test cases covering: (1) one test case per AC (happy path), (2) edge case test cases (boundaries, empty inputs, max values), (3) negative test cases (invalid input, permission denied, system errors). For each: ID, linked AC, description, steps, expected result. Format as a markdown table.

aiTasks.name: Risk-Based Scope Advisor
aiTasks.objective: Identify the highest-risk areas to focus test effort on.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Test Manager with expertise in risk-based testing. Analyse this feature and ACs. Identify: (1) highest-risk areas by probability × impact, (2) areas where automated testing adds most value, (3) areas requiring manual exploratory testing. Suggest a test priority order: critical (must test) / important (should test) / optional (nice to test).

title: Task Breakdown
sub: Discrete implementation tasks per feature with traceability
lifecycle: Per feature — created during sprint planning, updated as work progresses
doel: Break a feature into discrete tasks (≤8h each) with traceability to stories and ACs, and mark which tasks can run in parallel.
note: Tasks exceeding 8h must be split. Mark parallel-executable tasks with [P]. Every task must trace to at least one story or AC.

aiTasks.name: Task Decomposer
aiTasks.objective: Break the feature into discrete tasks ≤8h with parallelism markers.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior Developer. Decompose this feature into implementation tasks: (1) Each task ≤8h — split larger ones, (2) Mark tasks that can run in parallel as [P], (3) For each task: affected files, linked story/AC, clear done-when criterion, (4) Sequence dependent tasks explicitly. Output as a task table + parallelism summary.

aiTasks.name: Traceability Validator
aiTasks.objective: Verify every AC and story has at least one implementing task and one test.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a QA Engineer. Review this task breakdown against the stories and ACs: (1) ACs with no implementing task? (2) Tasks with no linked AC (orphaned work)? (3) ACs with no test case? Output a traceability matrix and flag gaps as HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW.
